nodes.label: graphify build pipeline (9 steps)
nodes.rationale: Step 0 GitHub URL handling -> Step 1 install -> Step 2 detect -> Step 2.5 transcribe -> Step 3 extract (AST + semantic) -> Step 4 build/cluster -> Step 5 label -> Step 6 Obsidian/HTML -> Steps 6b-8 wiki/neo4j/falkordb/svg/graphml/mcp/benchmark -> Step 9 cleanup. Each step depends on the previous, and the user-facing CLIs `graphify query/path/explain/add/clone/merge-graphs/export/hook/claude` are invoked from specific steps or as opt-in subcommands.

nodes.label: graphify fast path: answer from existing graph.json
nodes.rationale: When graphify-out/graph.json exists and the user asks a natural-language codebase question, the skill jumps straight to graphify query/path/explain instead of re-detecting and re-extracting. Skips Steps 1-5. This is the dominant usage mode after the first build.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify query (BFS/DFS, --budget)
nodes.rationale: User-facing traversal CLI. Default BFS up to depth 3, --dfs for path tracing, --budget caps token output. Returns a scoped subgraph so answers are small compared to GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify path (shortest path between concepts)
nodes.rationale: User-facing CLI that returns the shortest path between two named concepts. Falls back to inline NetworkX shortest_path when the CLI is unavailable.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify explain (plain-language node explanation)
nodes.rationale: User-facing CLI that produces a 3-5 sentence explanation of one node plus its neighborhood, citing source_location for each connection.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify update (incremental re-extraction)
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts only new/changed files via detect_incremental. Code-only changes skip the LLM semantic pass (Part B) and run only AST; doc/paper/image changes require LLM. build_merge reconciles changed files via replace-on-re-extract rather than a dedup pass (#1344).

nodes.label: CLI: graphify add <url> (ingest URL)
nodes.rationale: Fetches a URL (YouTube, arXiv, PDF, image, web) into ./raw, then runs --update to merge it into the existing graph. Supported types are auto-detected.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify export (obsidian/wiki/html/neo4j/falkordb/svg/graphml)
nodes.rationale: Step 6 always emits HTML (unless --no-viz) and Obsidian when --obsidian is given; Steps 6b-8 emit the optional wiki, Neo4j, FalkorDB, SVG, GraphML, MCP server, and token-reduction benchmark based on the corresponding flag.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify --watch (folder watcher)
nodes.rationale: Long-running background process that debounces file events. Code-only changes trigger AST + rebuild + cluster (no LLM); doc/paper/image changes write a needs_update flag and notify the user to run /graphify --update.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify hook (post-commit rebuild)
nodes.rationale: Installs a git post-commit hook that diffs HEAD~1, re-runs AST on changed code files, and rebuilds graph.json + GRAPH_REPORT.md. Appends to existing hook rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify claude (CLAUDE.md integration)
nodes.rationale: Writes a '## graphify' section to the project's local CLAUDE.md so Claude Code consults the graph on every codebase question. Mirrors the always-on rule described in .agents/rules/graphify.md.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify clone (GitHub repo fetch)
nodes.rationale: Clones a GitHub repo into ~/.graphify/repos/<owner>/<repo> and reuses existing clones on repeat runs. Only the first step in cross-repo or monorepo flows.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify merge-graphs (cross-repo merge)
nodes.rationale: Merges multiple graph.json files into one cross-repo graph. Each merged node carries a 'repo' attribute so consumers can filter by origin.

nodes.label: CLI: graphify save-result (Q&A feedback loop)
nodes.rationale: Saves the user's question, the answer text, the type (query/path_query/explain), and the cited node labels back into the graph so the next --update extracts the Q&A as a node. Closes the feedback loop.

nodes.label: graphify extraction JSON schema
nodes.rationale: Nodes carry id, label, file_type (one of code/document/paper/image/rationale/concept), source_file, source_location, source_url, captured_at, author, contributor. Edges carry source, target, relation (calls/implements/references/cites/conceptually_related_to/shares_data_with/semantically_similar_to/rationale_for), confidence (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), confidence_score, source_file, source_location, weight. Hyperedges are top-level with id, label, nodes, relation (participate_in/implement/form), confidence, confidence_score, source_file.

nodes.label: Node ID format: {parent_dir}_{filename}_{entity}
nodes.rationale: Lowercase a-z0-9_ only. Only the immediate parent dir is used. CRITICAL: never append chunk/sequence suffixes; IDs must be deterministic from the label so the AST extractor and subagent produce the same ID.

nodes.label: Confidence rubric (EXTRACTED=1.0, INFERRED=0.55-0.95, AMBIGUOUS=0.1-0.3)
nodes.rationale: Models collapse continuous confidence to a bimodal distribution (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+), so the rubric uses a discrete ladder: 0.95 direct structural, 0.85 strong, 0.75 reasonable, 0.65 weak, 0.55 speculative. EXTRACTED is always 1.0; AMBIGUOUS 0.1-0.3. The rubric is shared between the top-level skill and the extraction-spec subagent prompt.

nodes.label: Honesty / audit trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS)
nodes.rationale: Never invent edges, never skip the corpus check warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion behind symbols, never run HTML viz on >5000 nodes without warning. The three-confidence-tag system is the substrate this rule operates on.

nodes.label: AST + semantic split (Part A / Part B / Part C)
nodes.rationale: Part A runs AST on code (deterministic, free); Part B dispatches subagents for docs/papers/images (LLM, costs tokens); Part C merges AST + semantic by id. Run A and B in parallel; only B is skipped for code-only corpora.

nodes.label: Community detection + god nodes + surprising connections
nodes.rationale: graphify uses community detection to surface cross-document connections. god_nodes and surprising_connections are computed during build; --cluster-only reruns this without re-extracting, and wiki export writes one article per community.

nodes.label: Outputs: graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md, graph.json, obsidian/, wiki/
nodes.rationale: Three primary outputs (interactive HTML, plain-language GRAPH_REPORT.md, raw graph.json) plus opt-in Obsidian vault and wiki. The .graphify_extract.json / .graphify_detect.json sidecars are deleted by Step 9 cleanup.

nodes.label: Semantic extraction cache (.graphify_cached.json)
nodes.rationale: check_semantic_cache is run before dispatching subagents; only uncached files trigger LLM work. save_semantic_cache persists new results so a subsequent --update only pays for changed docs. Stale .graphify_cached.json is deleted before merge to prevent merging prior-run leftovers (#1392).

nodes.label: Incremental update + build_merge (replace-on-re-extract)
nodes.rationale: build_merge reads graph.json directly without NetworkX round-trip to preserve edge direction. Changed files are reconciled by deleting their prior source_file from the base before merge; deleted files are pruned via prune_sources relativized to the build root (#1361).

nodes.label: Neo4j and FalkorDB export
nodes.rationale: Both produce cypher.txt via graphify export {neo4j,falkordb}, or push live via --push. Uses MERGE so re-runs are safe. FalkorDB prefers --push because GRAPH.QUERY runs one statement at a time.

nodes.label: Vocab-based query expansion (Step 0 of query.md)
nodes.rationale: The query CLI uses case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming/synonyms. Before traversal, build .vocab.txt from node labels and pick up to 12 tokens that semantically match the user's question. This prevents collapse to noise when the user uses different vocabulary than the graph labels.

nodes.label: Whisper-based video/audio transcription (Step 2.5)
nodes.rationale: Reads god-node labels, composes a one-sentence domain hint, exports GRAPHIFY_WHISPER_PROMPT, then runs transcribe_all. Transcripts are routed into the documents list for Step 3B. Generic fallback prompt when the corpus is video-only.
